name: SSRN 2242795 10-month SMA timing, SPY vs T-bills
hypothesis: A monthly rule that holds SPY when its month-end price is above its 10-month simple moving average, and T-bills otherwise, has a higher Sharpe ratio and a smaller drawdown than buy-and-hold in out-of-sample, walk-forward tests with realistic costs. The paper argues that reported advantages of such rules are overstated, so the prior expectation is a small or no advantage.
drafted_by: OMP agent (Claude Opus 5.5) from the Crossref abstract; full text not retained

paper_claims.quote: We argue that the reported performance of market timing strategies usually contains a considerable data-mining bias and ignores important market frictions.
To address these issues, we perform out-of-sample tests of these two timing models in which we account for realistic transaction costs.
Our findings reveal that the performance of market timing strategies is highly overstated, to say the least.
see, for example, the paper by M. Faber (2007) "A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation" published in the Journal of Wealth Management

our_reading.interpretation: The paper tests two rule families (moving average and time-series momentum) out of sample with transaction costs and concludes that in-sample results overstate performance. We test the moving-average rule in the Faber form that the abstract cites as the reference, and select the window out of sample with a walk-forward procedure, which is our approximation of the paper's out-of-sample test.
gaps: Full text is not retained (no open-access copy; SSRN blocks automated download), so the paper's exact index, sample period, window grid, selection rule and cost level are unknown.
The abstract gives no numeric results, so no reported metrics can be compared with ours.
The paper's selection objective for the out-of-sample test is unknown.
assumptions: Instrument SPY (total return through adjusted closes) from 1993, instead of the paper's index history.
Cash earns the 13-week T-bill yield (^IRX), forward-filled, accrued per trading day.
Decision at the last trading day close of each month; fill at the next session open.
Window grid 2..12 months, selected by in-window Sharpe on a rolling 10-year train window, applied to the next 2 years.
Costs per side: commission 0.5 bp, half-spread 0.5 bp, slippage 1 bp; stress test at 5x.
deviations: Time-series momentum rule from the paper is not tested in this spec.
Single instrument; the paper may use a different market and a longer sample.

entry.rule: At a month-end close, if the adjusted close is above the 10-month SMA of month-end closes (including the current month), hold SPY from the next open.

exit.rule: At a month-end close, if the adjusted close is at or below the SMA, sell SPY at the next open and hold T-bills.
